ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the quadrilateral $ABDC$, the diagonal $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $\angle ACD=136^\circ$, $\angle BCD=44^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle ADB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line DE$\perp$AB through point D intersecting the extension of AB at E, and draw DF$\perp$AC through point D intersecting the extension of AC at F, and draw DG$\perp$BC through point D at point G, as shown in the figure: \\
$\because$ $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $DE\perp AB$, $DF\perp AC$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAD=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAC$, $DE=DF$\\
$\because$ $\angle ACD=136^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DCF=180^\circ-\angle ACD=44^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle BCD=44^\circ$, $\angle ACB=\angle ACD-\angle BCD=92^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $CD$ bisects $\angle BCF$\\
$\because$ $DF\perp AC$, $DG\perp BC$\\
$\therefore$ $DF=DG$\\
$\therefore$ $DE=DG$\\
$\because$ $DE\perp AB$, $DG\perp BC$\\
$\therefore$ $BD$ bisects $\angle CBE$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DBE=\frac{1}{2}\angle CBE$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADB=\angle DBE-\angle BAD$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\angle CBE-\frac{1}{2}\angle BAC$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\left(\angle CBE-\angle BAC\right)$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\angle BCA$\\
$=\boxed{46^\circ}$.

raw_record.original_question: In the quadrilateral $ABDC$, the diagonal $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $\angle ACD=136^\circ$, and $\angle BCD=44^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle ADB$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line $DE\perp AB$ through point $D$ intersecting the extension of $AB$ at $E$, draw $DF\perp AC$ through point $D$ intersecting the extension of $AC$ at $F$, and draw $DG\perp BC$ through point $D$ at point $G$, as shown in the figure: \\
$\because$ $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $DE\perp AB$, $DF\perp AC$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAD=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAC$, $DE=DF$\\
$\because$ $\angle ACD=136^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DCF=180^\circ-\angle ACD=44^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle BCD=44^\circ$, $\angle ACB=\angle ACD-\angle BCD=92^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $CD$ bisects $\angle BCF$\\
$\because$ $DF\perp AC$, $DG\perp BC$\\
$\therefore$ $DF=DG$\\
$\therefore$ $DE=DG$\\
$\because$ $DE\perp AB$, $DG\perp BC$\\
$\therefore$ $BD$ bisects $\angle CBE$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DBE=\frac{1}{2}\angle CBE$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADB=\angle DBE-\angle BAD$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\angle CBE-\frac{1}{2}\angle BAC$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}(\angle CBE-\angle BAC)$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\angle BCA$\\
$=\boxed{46^\circ}$

Image description: In the figure, A is at the lower left, C is at the upper left, D is at the upper right, B is at the lower right, and the quadrilateral is connected in the order A-B-D-C; line segment AD is the diagonal from A to D, line segment CB goes from C to B, and it can be seen from the figure that ray CB is located inside ∠ACD.
Reasoning: Because CB is inside ∠ACD, ∠ACB = ∠ACD − ∠BCD = 136° − 44° = 92°. Extend AC past C to a point F, then ∠DCF = 180° − 136° = 44°, and ∠BCD = 44°, so CD bisects the exterior angle at C of triangle ABC. The problem gives that AD bisects ∠BAC, that is, AD is the internal angle bisector at A. By the concurrency property of internal and external angle bisectors, D is also on the exterior angle bisector at B. Let AB be extended past B to E, then BD bisects exterior angle ∠CBE. Let ∠BAC = A, then ∠ABC = 180° − A − 92°, so exterior angle ∠CBE = 180° − ∠ABC = A + 92°. Therefore ∠DBE = (A + 92°)/2. At the same time, AD bisects ∠BAC, so ∠BAD = A/2. According to the positional relationship of AD and BD with respect to line AB in the figure, ∠ADB = ∠DBE − ∠BAD = (A + 92°)/2 − A/2 = 46°.
